text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3% today as oil prices jumped on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, sending U.S. crude up sharply and lifting the stock alongside it. The company benefits directly when crude prices rise—higher oil prices mean higher revenues and profits from production and refining operations.

The rally fits into a broader two-week surge of over 15% that tracks a steep climb in oil prices themselves. Tanker rates have also spiked significantly, which increases the *real* cost to move physical oil globally (adding roughly $38 per barrel to delivered cost), further tightening supply conditions and supporting crude values. For an integrated oil producer and refiner like ConocoPhillips, both higher crude prices and the squeeze on physical supply logistics work in its favor.
